doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Advice, listening and the record business
title: When they let him do it his way, it sold; songs chosen for money
summary: His early Chess and Checker records sold because he did what he wanted; songs were sometimes chosen because someone held a piece.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Have you ever had an experience like that with a record company?
You mean to do what I wanted to do?

Yeah! When I first went with Chess and Checker! They let me do what I wanted to do and you know what? And the record sold. I mean, they sold. And anytime they've let me do what I exactly wanted to do, the record sold. When I did it exactly how I wanted to, it sold. Yeah. You know. And I'm going to do that again and eventually, if -- if I don't do it with a company, I'm going to do it myself. Me and my wife and the rest of the group. You know, you know. [laughter] Yeah.
Has a record company ever asked you to record a particular song -­
-- or do material that you didn't -­
-- feel comfortable with, didn't wanna do?
Wasn't a point of not feeling comfortable. They wanted to do it because someone had a piece of it.
Yeah, sure. I mean, there's always some kind of funky motive, you know, there's never any honesty to this stuff. You know? Let's be honest, you know, and -- and do the record right. You know.
